findings: Verified fail-closed quarantine: all six legacy model workflows are workflow_dispatch-only on the pilot ref, pin destination_branch to the single authorized branch, gate on vars.PILOT_REMOTE_RESEARCH_ENABLED, run with contents:read and persist-credentials:false, use SHA-pinned actions, and unconditionally exit 1 before any model work; results-validate is if:false. Unset var, missing interpreter, or failed verify all fail the job with nothing published.

Verified identity bindings: workflow_boundary.verify requires an exact 40-hex source equal to git rev-parse HEAD and the hardcoded destination branch; workflow inputs reach it only via env vars (no shell interpolation); audit additionally binds current branch and clean working tree.

Verified append-only compare-and-swap publish: re-audit of exact source, remote tip must equal explicit --expected-remote pin, pin must be ancestor of source (fast-forward only), push uses --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected> which is a server-side atomic expected-old check; concurrent remote moves in either direction are refused and errors raise without retry.

Verified persistent-artifact hygiene in check_pilot_publication.audit: per-commit path allowlists, results/staged/.private component refusal, extension allowlist, regular-blob mode check, 1.5MB/NUL binary refusal, credential-pattern scan, notebook outputs/execution_count refusal, merge and dirty-tree refusal; contaminated-ancestry check fails closed on any non-1 return code including missing objects.

Verified preservation of scientific approvals: resolution doc keeps original responses versioned, states REQUEST_CHANGES is not approval, preserves the coordinator's completed APPROVE at 9a4e0bf with original snapshot checks, and keeps publication/future profiles under follow-up review; nothing in the supplied source contradicts this and no scientific receipt logic is altered.

Non-blocking: the mode check `git ls-tree <commit> -- <name>` treats name as a pathspec with wildcard matching; a literal filename containing glob characters (e.g. tests/z?.py alongside a regular tests/z1.py that sorts first) could report another entry's 100644 mode while `git show <commit>:<name>` reads the literal symlink, evading the non-regular-blob refusal. Contrived (requires the reviewed publisher to author it); fix by using ls-tree -z and comparing the returned path to name exactly, or a :(literal) pathspec.

Non-blocking: notebook screening checks cells' outputs/execution_count but not attachments (base64 payloads in markdown cells) or notebook/cell metadata, which can carry embedded data past the size/binary checks.
Non-blocking: commit messages in BASE..tip are never scanned; credential/private-data screening applies only to blob contents.

Informational (fail-closed but worth documenting): audit skips any path where `git cat-file -e` fails, conflating deletion with other object-lookup failures; publish has no bootstrap path when the remote branch does not yet exist (ls-remote must return exactly one existing ref).
Review basis: source-only analysis of the supplied files; no tests were executed and no repository state beyond the provided source was inspected.
